title: Fix streaming cadence regression in fast tier by prioritizing decode under mixed load
author: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Context: After landing tiered batching defaults behind the flag, we saw a regression in streaming cadence specifically for batching_tier=fast on mixed workloads (streaming chat + non-streaming completions arriving concurrently). TTFT was stable, but inter-token latency (ITL) and token jitter increased, making clients perceive “bursty” streams. Root cause: our fast-tier scheduler weights biased toward admitting/processing new prefills under sustained arrival, starving decode slices for already-started streams. This is particularly noticeable when queue delay is kept low (fast tier) because requests are admitted quickly and we keep paying prefill costs while decode work piles up.

Change summary: (1) Adjust scheduler prioritization so that when streaming responses are active, decode gets a bounded priority boost and cannot be starved by new prefill work. (2) Add a regression test that reproduces the mixed-load scenario and asserts cadence/jitter bounds for fast tier.

Implementation details: We introduce a “streaming decode guardrail” that (a) enforces a minimum decode service share per scheduling tick when there are active streaming sequences, and (b) caps prefill tokens processed per tick in the presence of active decodes. Concretely, the fast-tier mapping sets decode_priority_boost=1.35 (previously 1.0) and enables prefill_budget_tokens_per_tick (new) derived from GPU SKU and expected concurrency bucket; when active_streaming>0, prefill work is scheduled only up to the budget, after which we drain decode until the decode service share target is met. This preserves TTFT while restoring steady token cadence.

Testing: Adds a deterministic scheduler test harness case that starts N=2 streaming chats and injects M=4 short non-streaming requests at 50ms offsets. The test asserts: (i) ITL p95 for streaming sequences <= 85ms (fast tier), (ii) max inter-token gap <= 200ms under the mixed load pattern, and (iii) no increase in timeouts/cancellations. The test is designed to fail on the prior behavior.

Rollout: Safe as a hotfix because it only affects fast tier behavior and is gated behind the existing tiered-batching feature flag. No config schema changes. We should still watch token-cadence and queue-delay panels during the next ramp.

Follow-ups: Consider propagating the same guardrail to standard tier with a smaller boost once we’ve validated perf impact; also consider adding an explicit “streaming cadence” SLO metric to perf-canary so we don’t regress on future scheduler refactors.
commits: runtime/scheduler: add streaming decode guardrail and prefill budget
runtime/tiers: tune fast tier decode priority boost
tests/scheduler: add mixed streaming + non-streaming cadence regression case
docs/internal: add notes on cadence metric interpretation
review_conversation: Mateo Alvarez: The diagnosis matches what we saw in canary. Please be explicit about the starvation condition: sustained arrival of prefills + low queue delay + decode weight not enforced. Also ensure the boost doesn’t tank TTFT in the simple streaming-only case.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Updated description and added a streaming-only assertion to ensure TTFT delta stays within +3%. The guardrail only activates when active_streaming>0 and there is concurrent prefill pressure; streaming-only stays effectively unchanged.
Marcus Reed: I like the prefill budget concept. Can we make the budget derived from concurrency buckets so it doesn’t underutilize on high-end SKUs?
Sofia Ivanova (author): Yes—budget now uses the existing workload signal (concurrency_bucket) and a per-SKU multiplier. Added a unit test for A100 vs L4 mapping to avoid accidental regressions.
Julian Moore: For the regression test, please surface the cadence metrics in the test output (p50/p95 ITL, max gap). It’ll help when debugging flakes.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Done. Test now logs the summary table and writes a JSON artifact for CI to collect on failure.
Sean Gallagher: Any SLO implications? fast tier p95 latency is sensitive; ensure we’re not increasing end-to-end p95 just to improve cadence.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Measured on the mixed-load harness: end-to-end p95 changed by +1.8% (within noise), ITL p95 improved ~28%. Added note to rollout watchlist.
Mateo Alvarez: Approved. Let’s merge and monitor during the next ramp.
release_notes: Runtime: Fix streaming cadence regression for batching_tier=fast under mixed streaming + non-streaming load by enforcing decode service share; adds regression test to prevent recurrence.
